clue.text: Awkward conditions for section of orchestra

definitions.meaning: ... attached to a deal are unwelcome terms imposed on it
the violins, violas, cellos and basses together

explanation.definitionFit: Conditions tied to an offer are called strings, and the bowed instruments form the orchestra's string section.

clue.text: Minor actor has to drink wine

parts.note: sup means to drink in sips
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A bit-part player is drinking on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporting performer plays below the leads, so a lesser cast member is a support.

clue.text: Letter from America?

parts.note: reads as a posted message or the radio series, but means someone in the US who lets property

explanation.surface: Correspondence sent across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' means one who lets, rents out, houses; the US word for an estate agent is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An American real-estate agent, who sells and lets homes.

clue.text: A score in the nick

definitions.meaning: a cut marked to keep count, or a point scored

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a tally mark or point and a small cut in an edge.

clue.text: Monday's inferior time

definitions.note: read as Monday is, the 's standing for is

parts.note: second, as in second-rate
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Mondays are the worst part of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monday's' is read as 'Monday is': in a week counted from Sunday, Monday is the next after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting the week from Sunday, Monday falls in place number two.

clue.text: Go miles out of the way in France

indicators.note: letters sent out of their usual way are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a long detour while travelling in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the way' rearranges GO and MILES; the definition 'in France' is loose, pointing at a place located in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in west-central France, famous for porcelain.

clue.text: Holds out models of foot

definitions.meaning: wooden shapes on which a shoemaker forms shoes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means endures, and also names a cobbler's foot-shaped forms.

clue.text: In Spain, Mary has John in for tea?

indicators.note: John is put inside Mary, the name containing him

parts.note: Maria is the Spanish form of Mary
Juan is the Spanish form of John

explanation.surface: In Spain, Mary invites John in for a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Spain' applies to both names; 'tea' is old slang for cannabis, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea was period slang for cannabis, the drug smoked as a joint.

clue.text: Led game into disrepute, but shone a bit

indicators.note: bringing the words into disrepute leaves their letters in disarray

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sportsman shamed the sport, though he had moments of brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into disrepute' rearranges LED GAME; 'but' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To glimmer is to give off a faint flash of light briefly.

clue.text: New York roses can be sensational

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Roses from New York can be a knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges NY and ROSES; 'sensational' is used in its old sense of relating to sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can describe things perceived through the senses.

clue.text: Features editor?

parts.note: read not as a newspaper post but as someone who edits facial features

explanation.surface: A job title on a magazine staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A features editor runs a newspaper's feature pages; the question mark lets 'features' mean a face, which a cosmetic surgeon reshapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic surgeon who remodels the nose, chin and other parts of the face.

clue.text: See 9
House isn't in order yet it is brighter than the rest

indicators.note: the letters are put into a fresh order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A house is not tidy, yet it still dazzles beside its neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' looks like tidiness but rearranges the nine letters of HOUSE ISN'T; 'yet it' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass others in brilliance is to shine more than all of them.

clue.text: Jet set member with a good memory

definitions.text: Jet set member with a good memory

parts.words: Jet set member with a good memory
parts.note: reads as a rich socialite, but means a large aircraft and also an elephant, the animal that never forgets

explanation.surface: A glamorous traveller who never forgets a face.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbo jet is the Boeing 747, and Jumbo was a famous elephant; elephants are proverbially said never to forget.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a wide-bodied airliner and, by the circus elephant's name, any elephant.

clue.text: Was it carried for an old flame?

definitions.text: Was it carried for an old flame?

parts.words: Was it carried for an old flame?
parts.note: the idiom of carrying a light for a past love, with 'flame' also meaning fire

explanation.surface: Someone still pining for a former sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'carry a torch' for someone is to love them unrequited; a torch also carries a literal flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held burning light, carried in the idiom for lasting unreturned love.

clue.text: Pointed statement from a Chinaman who encountered Naomi's daughter-in-law

parts.note: Ho is a common Chinese surname, in the dated language of the clue
met means came across
in the Bible, Ruth married Naomi's son

explanation.surface: A remark made after a Chinese man meets a biblical woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses a dated term; 'from' and 'who' link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An unwelcome but accurate remark aimed at someone's faults.

clue.text: Cowardly darts lady throws

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman at the oche is accused of timidity as she throws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throws' fits the darts picture but rearranges DARTS LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dastardly once meant timid and craven, later wicked and underhand.

clue.text: Betting odds recital-opening out

parts.note: SP is the starting price in horse-race betting
a reading is a recital of a text

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's odds sheet and a concert debut.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the British term for the odds when a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfolding or extending over a wider area.

clue.text: He is chained in his office…

definitions.text: He is chained in his office

parts.words: He is chained in his office
parts.note: sounds like a prisoner at work, but describes the ceremonial chain worn by a civic head

explanation.surface: A clerk shackled to his desk.
explanation.walkthrough: A city's civic head wears a chain of office; 'chained in his office' means wearing it while in post.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial head of a city corporation, such as London's, who wears a gold chain of office.

clue.text: Once round track, victory over gravity for peewit

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit above the next one

parts.note: a lap is one circuit
a win
g is the symbol for gravity's acceleration

explanation.surface: A bird circles the track and triumphs over gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Peewit is the call-based name for the crested plover of fields and marshes.

clue.text: Narration — using indefinite article

indicators.note: the letters have no fixed order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A story told using 'a' or 'an'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indefinite article' looks like grammar ('a', 'an'); 'indefinite' rearranges ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed spoken account of events is a narration.

clue.text: … a small office-section but highly skilled

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a section of an office

explanation.surface: A small corner of the office turns out to be very capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone very proficient at a task is expert at it.

clue.text: As blind as Huxley in Gaza?

definitions.text: As blind as Huxley in Gaza?

parts.words: As blind as Huxley in Gaza?
parts.note: points to the Aldous Huxley novel whose title borrows Milton's line about Samson, blinded in Gaza

explanation.surface: A question about sightlessness in a famous novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldous Huxley's novel 'Eyeless in Gaza' takes its title from Milton's Samson Agonistes.
explanation.definitionFit: Without sight, having no organs of vision.

clue.text: Noted lofty, arboreal site of cradle

definitions.text: Noted lofty, arboreal site of cradle

parts.words: Noted lofty, arboreal site of cradle
parts.note: the nursery rhyme Rock-a-bye Baby puts the cradle high up among the branches

explanation.surface: A famous high perch in a tree for a baby's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, the baby's cradle sits 'on the tree top' until the bough breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest branches of a tree, where the rhyme's cradle rocks.

clue.text: Changing the topic? Embroiderer's not, we hear

definitions.note: 'not' said aloud is knot, so this reads as an embroiderer's knot

indicators.note: changing the word means altering the order of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shifts the subject, denying they embroider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges TOPIC; the definition relies on 'not' heard as 'knot', since a picot is a small ornamental loop of thread on an edging.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative loop of twisted thread worked along the edge of lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Deep breath?

parts.note: deep is a poetic word for the ocean, so a breath of the deep is wind off the water

explanation.surface: A big inhalation before a plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The deep' is a literary name for the sea, so its breath is a wind blowing in from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A light wind blowing onshore from the ocean.

clue.text: Lady over the road has broken piece of pottery

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman across the street has a shattered pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sherd is a variant spelling of shard, a fragment of broken ceramic.

clue.text: Kind of star to show a Dior creation

indicators.note: a new creation is something made up out of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity model shows off a Dior design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creation' suits the fashion picture but rearranges A DIOR; 'to show' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio star is a celestial source of strong radio waves, or a broadcasting celebrity.

clue.text: I turned round in barge

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters are turned round into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turns about inside a canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges I and TURNED; 'barge' is the verb, with 'in' as a link that also hints at barge in.
explanation.definitionFit: To push one's way rudely into a place or conversation without being invited.

clue.text: Lived in Little India, a foreign world!

parts.note: Ind is a short, old-fashioned form of India
Welt is the German word for world

explanation.surface: Someone recalls living in a small Indian quarter abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals the shortening of India; 'foreign' points to German, where world is Welt.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell within a place, as a spirit within a body, is to inhabit it.

clue.text: Festivity enjoyed with guest at fabulous table

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
had, as in had a good time

explanation.surface: A guest at a lavish banquet enjoys the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fabulous table' is King Arthur's legendary Round Table, so a guest there is one of his knights.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad was the purest knight of the legendary Round Table of Arthurian fable.

clue.text: Here, in Derbyshire, one takes a shine to work

parts.note: gloss is a sheen or lustre
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone in a Derbyshire town takes a liking to their job.
explanation.walkthrough: Glossop is a market town in Derbyshire, an English county; 'one takes a' links the pieces, and 'takes a shine to' misleads as 'grows fond of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossop is a town in the High Peak area of the county.
